curation.lead:
According to UK Companies House filings and SEC proxy disclosures, Alessandro Benedetti (born July 1961, Italian national, Swiss resident in Lugano) is a Geneva-based financier, founding partner of Schwarzfield, and CEO of SAE Capital Ltd [Finding #861][Finding #1632]. The same records reveal directorships across at least seven jurisdictions, including Attali Investment Partners Ltd, Asherco LLP, SPQR Capital Holdings S.A., and the NYSE-listed Equus Total Return Inc., where he served as Executive Chairman from June 2011 to June 2014 [Finding #842][Finding #847]. He is referenced as Jeffrey Epstein’s Paris neighbor in a December 2011 email from Reid Weingarten, who describes him as “your Italian jewish neighbor on ave. foch” [EFTA00925685][Finding #814].

Benedetti’s career centers on cross-border dealmaking. According to press and UK court records, he brokered the 2005 acquisition of Wind Telecomunicazioni SpA for Naguib Sawiris, reported at approximately €12 billion, and subsequently sued Sawiris for a one-third stake in the proceeds before losing at the UK Supreme Court in 2013 [Finding #861]. Epstein’s scheduling records place Benedetti first on a September 2013 “Paris List” of fourteen contacts [EFTA02575400][Finding #835], and a January 28, 2019 email shows Epstein inquiring about him through Eduardo Teodorani at CNH Industrial with the one-line query “Allesandro benedetti?” [EFTA02628256][Finding #518].

According to a February 2020 Wall Street Journal investigation, Rajeev Misra of SoftBank paid Benedetti $500,000 in April 2015, routed via Standard Chartered Bank to Barkmere Group Ltd (BVI), to coordinate a covert campaign against internal rivals Nikesh Arora and Alok Sama [Finding #776][Finding #740]. According to the same reporting, the operation involved Nicolas Giannakopoulos, a Swiss intermediary identified by WSJ as having SCL Group ties, and included a shareholder pressure campaign and negative press placements [Finding #785]. According to WSJ, Benedetti disclosed the arrangement to the paper after a compensation dispute with Misra [Finding #774]. Epstein’s emails show him querying both Brad Karp about representing Misra and Teodorani about Benedetti within a 72-hour window in late January 2019 [Finding #733][Finding #988].

Documented in Epstein scheduling records as a Paris contact from 2011 to 2019, and separately identified in a February 2020 Wall Street Journal investigation as the coordinator of a covert campaign against SoftBank executives on behalf of Rajeev Misra.

sections.title: The Avenue Foch Connection
sections.content:
The documentary trail places Benedetti within Epstein’s Paris network across an eight-year span from 2011 to 2019 [Finding #1244]. The earliest record is Weingarten’s December 9, 2011 email to Epstein asking “did we ever talk about allesandro Benedetti, your Italian jewish neighbor on ave. foch?” [EFTA00925685][Finding #814]. The possessive “your” indicates Weingarten treated Benedetti as already known to Epstein through the Avenue Foch property — the same street as Epstein’s 22 Avenue Foch Paris residence [Finding #814]. Cross-reference of the email thread shows Epstein engaged on other topics but did not respond in writing to the Benedetti question, which analysts of the thread characterize as either a prior phone discussion or a preference to avoid a written response [Finding #814].

By September 2013, Benedetti appeared in Epstein’s Paris scheduling records. Groff’s “Paris List” [EFTA02575400] places “Alesandro de benedetti” first among fourteen contacts, a roster that included Ariane de Rothschild, Wojtek Fibak of Fine Arts Investments, Margherita Campella Della Spina, a “Sultan,” and conductor Frederic Chaslin [Finding #835]. Records show the same day’s schedule [EFTA02297224] lists the Benedetti reminder alongside an 8:30am breakfast with Ian Osborne (a Peter Thiel intermediary), an 11:30am lunch with Larry Summers, and a 1:00pm meeting with Richard Kahn and Darren Indyke, before a 9:55pm Air France departure for Paris [Finding #849][Finding #734]. Duplicate reminders on September 26 and October 7 [EFTA02575276][EFTA02576024] record repeated scheduling around Benedetti during the trip cycle [Finding #519].

The final documented reference is Epstein’s January 28, 2019 email to Eduardo Teodorani at CNH Industrial containing the single-line inquiry “Allesandro benedetti?” [EFTA02628256][Finding #518]. The query arrived two days after Epstein asked Brad Karp about representing Rajeev Misra, and within the same week Weingarten discussed the “Softbank caper” with Epstein [Finding #733][Finding #988]. Analysis of the 72-hour window indicates Epstein was tracking the SoftBank matter through Italian corporate channels rather than contacting Benedetti directly [Finding #778].

sections.title: Corporate Architecture Across Jurisdictions
sections.content:
Cross-reference of UK Companies House, SEC proxy filings, and ICIJ records indicates Benedetti’s corporate footprint spans at least seven jurisdictions — UK, Switzerland, France, Italy, BVI, Cyprus, and Malta — with public-facing advisory vehicles on one tier and offshore holding entities on another [Finding #842][Finding #861]. According to UK filings and MarketScreener listings, Benedetti founded SAE Capital Ltd in January 2007, chairs Schwarzfield SA from February 2013, and serves as director of SPQR Capital Holdings SA from August 2010 [Finding #1633][Finding #1632]. SEC proxy filings for Equus Total Return Inc. (NYSE: EQS, CIK 878932), where he served as Executive Chairman from June 2011 to June 2014, itemize eight concurrent directorships and record personal ownership of over 100,000 shares plus 400,000 held through EB Finance S.A., an entity of which Benedetti disclaimed beneficial ownership in the DEF 14A disclosures [Finding #847].

The UK tier contains four Companies House appointments [Finding #842]. Asherco LLP (OC379532), active since October 2012, shows a sequential rotation through two BVI corporate members: Youngstown Investments Group Ltd (BVI 1688567, November 2014–November 2021) and Satsu Finance Ltd (BVI 1583501, November 2021–March 2023), both registered at the same PO Box 3483, R.G. Hodge Plaza, Wickhams Cay 1, Road Town, Tortola [Finding #843]. After the BVI members departed, Israeli national Dotan Moshe (March 2023–July 2024) served briefly before being replaced by Mathieu Villaume of Luxembourg [Finding #843]. Analysis of the rotation pattern indicates a structure that maintains a UK regulatory presence while cycling corporate members through a shared BVI registered-agent address [Finding #843].

According to UK Companies House records, Attali Investment Partners Ltd (UK 07138407, January 2010–December 2015) links Benedetti to Franco-Italian political networks [Finding #844][Finding #1633]. Records show the entity is named for Jacques Attali, former senior adviser to President Mitterrand and founding president of the EBRD, and was co-directed by Bertrand Gauquelin des Pallieres (born November 1966, French, resident in Rome) until both resigned in the same month in December 2015 and were replaced by Methorios Capital LLP as corporate director [Finding #844]. Cross-reference with Wall Street Journal reporting on the SoftBank matter indicates that des Pallieres, a former Deutsche Bank trader who had worked under Misra, later introduced Misra to Benedetti for the operation described in that reporting [Finding #740].

According to WSJ reporting, the offshore tier includes Barkmere Group Ltd (BVI), the vehicle through which Misra’s $500,000 payment was routed, together with Barkmere Limited (Cyprus) [Finding #776]. According to the ICIJ Paradise Papers, Benedetti is identified as shareholder of Tree of Life Limited (Malta, C67345, incorporated October 2014), registered at Via delle Serre N. 9/A, Florence, with cross-reference of UK Companies House filings confirming this entity is distinct from the Northzone VC associate of a similar name [Finding #776][Finding #1644]. According to OCCRP Aleph, a separate Cyprus entity of the same name (HE 279303, incorporated December 2010, dissolved January 2016) sits sixteen months before the Malta entity’s incorporation, a chronology the Aleph record characterizes as a possible jurisdictional migration from Cyprus to Malta [Finding #833].

sections.title: The SoftBank Campaign, as Reported by WSJ
sections.content:
According to the February 2020 Wall Street Journal investigation, in January 2015 Rajeev Misra — then a senior SoftBank executive positioning for leadership of what became the Vision Fund — met Benedetti in London to commission an operation against his internal rivals SoftBank president Nikesh Arora and chief strategy officer Alok Sama [Finding #740][Finding #785]. According to the same reporting, Bertrand des Pallieres, a former Deutsche Bank trader who had worked under Misra before relocating to Rome, made the introduction [Finding #740]. According to WSJ, by April 2015 Misra had paid $500,000 via Standard Chartered Bank to Barkmere Group Ltd, the BVI entity controlled by Benedetti [Finding #776]. According to the same report, Misra’s spokesman characterized the transfer as an “oil investment,” a characterization the WSJ report treats as disputed [Finding #776].

According to WSJ, the alleged campaign ran on multiple tracks [Finding #785]. According to the same reporting, an attempt in Tokyo to compromise Arora using women and hidden cameras did not succeed [Finding #785]. According to WSJ, Benedetti subcontracted Nicolas Giannakopoulos, a Swiss operative the paper identifies as having ties to Cambridge Analytica’s parent SCL Group, to distribute leaked banking records and organize a nominal shareholder campaign [Finding #740]. According to the report, K2 Intelligence was engaged to investigate Arora and Sama and in turn retained London PR firm Powerscourt Group to place the resulting material [Finding #785]. According to WSJ, by September 2015 Giannakopoulos had engaged freelance journalist Mark Hollingsworth, and in October 2015 The Independent published an article on Arora [Finding #785]. According to the same reporting, the shareholder pressure campaign launched in November 2015, with the first formal letter arriving in January 2016 [Finding #785]. According to WSJ, Arora resigned in June 2016 and Sama departed in April 2019 [Finding #785]. According to the report, the alleged operation used the code name “Mr. West” for Arora, Misra provided a dedicated cellphone for operational communications, and meetings were conducted at London’s Bulgari Hotel and Zurich’s Hotel Baur au Lac in November 2017 [Finding #740].

According to WSJ, the arrangement collapsed over compensation [Finding #774]. According to the reporting, Benedetti expected substantially more than the initial $500,000 — a share of Misra’s SoftBank earnings and appointment to lead the Vision Fund’s London office — and when neither materialized he recorded conversations with Misra detailing the alleged plans against Arora and Sama [Finding #774]. According to WSJ, Benedetti provided the recordings and documentation to the paper, which published its investigation in February 2020 [Finding #774]. According to the same reporting, a Shearman & Sterling probe commissioned in 2018 was inconclusive [Finding #785]. Cross-reference of the WSJ account with UK Companies House and Paradise Papers records indicates a pattern of multi-layered subcontracting, BVI payment channels, PR firm placements, and shareholder letter campaigns consistent with the corporate architecture documented for Benedetti’s entities [Finding #740][Finding #843].

sections.title: Epstein and the SoftBank Convergence
sections.content:
A cluster of documentary evidence from late January 2019 links Epstein’s prior Paris relationship with Benedetti to the emerging SoftBank matter. Around January 25, 2019, Weingarten discussed the “Softbank caper” with Epstein [Finding #733]. On January 26, Epstein asked Brad Karp of Paul, Weiss about representing Misra [Finding #733][Finding #988]. On January 28, Epstein emailed Eduardo Teodorani at CNH Industrial with the one-line inquiry “Allesandro benedetti?” [EFTA02628256][Finding #518]. Records show three separate contacts — Weingarten, Karp, and Teodorani — queried within a 72-hour window on related facets of the same matter [Finding #988].

According to the available documentary record, Epstein is not a party to the original campaign against Arora and Sama [Finding #778]. By January 2019, however, he was inquiring about the individual WSJ later identified as the coordinator (Benedetti), exploring legal representation for the reported beneficiary (Misra), and discussing the broader matter with his own counsel [Finding #733]. Analysis of the 72-hour inquiry pattern indicates Epstein was tracking the SoftBank situation in real time through multiple intermediaries, with the Teodorani routing indicating an indirect rather than direct approach to Benedetti [Finding #778][Finding #1244]. Analysis of the correspondence indicates Epstein’s choice of Teodorani as channel, rather than contacting Benedetti directly, is consistent with a relationship that had changed character by early 2019, although the record does not specify when or why [Finding #778].

sections.title: Position in the Paris Network
sections.content:
Benedetti’s placement within Epstein’s Paris correspondence ecosystem illuminates the structure of that network. The September 2013 “Paris List” [EFTA02575400] is one of the few documents that maps Epstein’s Parisian social circle in a single snapshot [Finding #835]. Records show Benedetti appears first, followed by names that include “Ariane” (likely Ariane de Rothschild), Wojtek Fibak of Fine Arts Investments, Margherita Campella Della Spina (arriving by train September 27), a “Sultan in Paris Sun Sept 29,” and conductor Frederic Chaslin [Finding #835][Finding #519]. Examination of the list indicates it combines the social registers Epstein cultivated — finance, art, European aristocracy, and Gulf wealth — with Benedetti positioned among the financial contacts [Finding #835].

According to UK Companies House, the Attali Investment Partners directorship anchors Benedetti in Franco-Italian political networks [Finding #844]. Records reveal Jacques Attali as a former senior adviser to President Mitterrand and founding president of the EBRD [Finding #1633]. Cross-reference of Benedetti’s directorships indicates his position on Attali’s investment vehicle placed him at the intersection of French political access and Italian financial networks, a profile consistent with the cross-border intermediaries documented elsewhere in the Epstein Paris records [Finding #1633][Finding #849]. According to UK Companies House and DOJ Vol 11 records, Benedetti’s earlier role as president of M Finances SAS (Paris, 2000–2001) and director of Vendome Investments Ltd (UK, 2005–2011) establishes a Paris-London axis predating the Epstein correspondence by roughly a decade [Finding #1632]. According to UK Supreme Court and press records, his 2005 brokerage of Naguib Sawiris’s Wind Telecomunicazioni acquisition, for which he was separately investigated by Roman prosecutors in 2008 and which produced the UK Supreme Court case Benedetti v Sawiris (2013), illustrates the scale of dealmaking that preceded the Paris contacts period [Finding #861].
